body.p: Applicant has thoroughly reviewed the outstanding non-final Office Action dated December 14, 2023, and this reply is believed to be fully responsive thereto. Claims 2-14, 17, and 19-22 are pending. Claims 2, 13-14, 17 and 19 are amended. Claims 21-22 are new. No new subject matter has been added. Applicant respectfully requests that all claims be allowed and this application pass to issuance in view of the following remarks.

Applicant gratefully appreciates the indication that claim 20 would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. In order to expedite prosecution, new independent claim 21 includes the subject matter of claim 20 and its base and intervening claims. Accordingly, new independent claim 21 and its dependent claims are believed to be in condition for allowance.

Claims 2-7, 9-10, and 11-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Pub. 2009/0005675 ("Grunwald") in view of U.S. Patent 6,662,055 ("Prutchi"). Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Grunwald and Prutchi and further in view of U.S. Pub. 2015/0173829 ("Lichtenstein"). Claims 15-19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Grunwald and Prutchi and further in view of U.S. Pub. 2014/0142670 ("Radhakrishnan").

Without conceding to the propriety of this rejection, but rather to expedite prosecution, independent claim 2 is amended to recite "a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member; a sensor disposed at a distal end of the ring electrode and configured to detect and measure a physiological parameter in a patient's vasculature;

a first electrical conductor disposed within the inner lumen of the elongate member and connected to the ring electrode, the first electrical conductor configured to receive a first signal from the ring electrode and convey the first signal to a computing device; and a second electrical conductor disposed within the inner lumen of the elongate member and connected to the sensor, the second electrical conductor configured to receive a second signal from the sensor and convey the second signal to the computing device... wherein the first electrical conductor includes a distal portion and a proximal portion, and the distal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet is more flexible than the proximal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet." Grunwald, Prutchi, Lichtenstein, and Radhakrishnan, either taken alone or together, fail to disclose or make obvious each and every feature recited in amended independent claim 2.

For instance, the Office Action acknowledges that Grunwald and Prutchi both fail to disclose a ring electrode. The Office Action relies on Radhakrishnan to teach a ring electrode. However, Radhakrishnan fails to disclose or suggest at least a ring electrode extending from the distal end of an elongate member. Rather, Radhakrishnan discloses an electrode 114 including a main body 140 having a ring structure, wherein the main body 140 is entirely within the lead body 108 (i.e., the main body 140 is not exposed on the exterior of the lead 106), as shown in Figure 2 (see also paragraph [0035]) .

Accordingly, since Radhakrishnan does not cure the deficiencies of Grunwald and Prutchi, a primafacie case of obviousness cannot be established with respect to amended independent claim 2 and any claims depending therefrom. Reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection is therefore respectfully requested.
New Claims
New independent claim 21 incorporates the allowable subject matter of claim 20. Accordingly, new independent claim 21 and its dependent claim 22 are believed to be in
condition for allowance. Moreover, none of the cited references, either taken alone or in combination, disclose or make obvious each and every feature of new claims 21 and 22.

Claims 2-20 have been rejected for obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854. Amended independent claim 2 now recites features, such as a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member, that are not recited in claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854 or disclosed in any of the cited references. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection of claims 2-20 is respectfully requested.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant submits that all claims are in condition for allowance, and an indication of such is earnestly solicited.

It is believed that all of the pending issues have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Further, Applicants declare that any amendments herein that are not specifically made for the purpose of patentability are made for other purposes, such as clarification, and that no such changes shall be construed as limiting the scope of the claims or the application of the Doctrine of Equivalents. Finally, nothing in this reply should be construed as an intent to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this reply, and the
amendment of any claim does not necessarily signify concession of unpatentability of the claim prior to its amendment.

It would be appreciated if the Examiner would telephone the undersigned attorney at 202-861-1500 concerning any questions related to this response in an effort to resolve any matter sill outstanding before issuing another action.
